main_text.p: cula, Sagittas pedibus calcant & trahunt præ vnis no-De Armis iudicium.stris Bombardis. Hoc fulmen & tonitru nullam Romanam aciem sustinere potuisse: vtique si grandiora illaVulgi sen-fu reiecta veterū. accederent & quassatoria tormenta. Hæc & plura ita differunt: quid rerum veterum aliquis bene gnarus? Habeat profecto, quod reponat, & quo refellat. Pri-Nostro,af-ferta & defensa.mum,quod missilia illa omnia eleuant, vereor vt vim eorum bene norint. Fundæ,quantulum à nostris bom-bardis vi & effectu (nam forma diuersissima) abierunt?Fundarū visio. Ridiculum hoc in primo auditu: sed mecum examina. E plumbo vtrumque telum est, nec magnitudine aut modo glandes valdè dispares: nec impetu aut violentiâImpeta[?] adsimiles bombardis. valdè vincantur Fundæ. Credere me iis oportet, qui vi-derunt,qui interfuerunt militiæ priscæ, & *Nō enim nunc, credo, tales.{*}cùm hæc arte & vsu valebant:ij ergo scribunt,quę componant cum bombardis eas,aut anteponant. De impetu,is tantus in emissâ perite fundâ, vt glans sæpè liquesceret in medio cursu,concepto igne.
Lucretius: ——plumbea vero Glans etiam longo cursu volucnda liquescit.
Ouidius: Non secus exarsit,quàm cùm Balearica plumbum Funda iacit. volat illud, & incandescit eundo, Et quos non habuit, sub nubibus inuenit ignes.
Lucanus: Inde faces & saxa volant,spatioque solutæ Aëris,& calido liquefactæ pondere glandes.
Statius: —— arsuras cali per inania glandes.Lib. vi.
Imò idem cum fulmine comparat: —— volucres imitantur fulgura glandes.
Poëtis fortasse fidem non habes? Philosophus accedat, noster Seneca: Aëra motus extenuat, & extenuatio ac-Nat.quæst. II.cap.LVIcendit. Sic liquescit excussa glans funda, & attritu aëris

page.notes: Left margin: show-through from the facing page, not transcribed. Doubtful: "Impeta" in the note beside "nec magnitudine aut modo" (read as Impetu or Impeta); "plumbum" in the Ouidius quotation (the scan looks like plumbum with a diaeresis-like mark). The Lucretius line "volucnda" looks like the printed form; "Aëris" is printed with a diaeresis. The verse lines of the quotations are set as one paragraph each, with printed line breaks kept as newlines.
